--- title: "[CauseSpecificCox]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Cause-specific Cox proportional-hazards model for competing risks. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_competing.py#L1660-L1890){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python CauseSpecificCox(cause, *, ties="efron", conf_level=0.95) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} In a competing-risks setting, a cause-specific hazard model answers "among subjects still event-free, what drives the rate of this particular event?" It does so by treating competing events as censoring: subjects who experience a different cause are removed from the risk set at the time of their competing event, and a standard Cox model is fitted on the re-coded data. This wrapper takes a multi-state `Surv` response and a target cause, automatically re-codes the competing events as censored, and delegates to `CoxPH`. All `CoxPH` features (stratification, frailty, robust standard errors, diagnostics, prediction) are available on the fitted object. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [cause]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The cause of interest. Can be a state label (string) matching one of the `states` in the `Surv` response, or an integer cause code (1-indexed). [ties]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["efron"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Tie-handling method passed to `CoxPH`: `"efron"` (default) or `"breslow"`. [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for coefficient intervals (default 0.95). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a cause-specific Cox model for PCM progression in the `mgus2` dataset: ::: {#43c8b607 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw mg = gw.load_dataset("mgus2", backend="polars") cr = gw.Outcome.first_event( endpoints={"pcm": ("ptime", "pstat"), "death": ("futime", "death")} ) csc = gw.CauseSpecificCox(cause="pcm").fit(cr, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=mg) csc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` CauseSpecificCox (cause-specific Cox model, cause='pcm', ties='efron') coef exp(coef) se(coef) z p age 0.01304 1.013 0.008259 1.579 0.1144 sexM -0.02514 0.9752 0.1885 -0.133 0.8939 n = 1384, events = 115 Likelihood ratio test = 2.682 on 2 df, p = 0.2616 ``` ::: ::: Compare cause-specific hazard ratios for both causes side by side: ::: {#3845db73 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} csc_death = gw.CauseSpecificCox(cause="death").fit(cr, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=mg) gw.tidy(csc, exponentiate=True, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

fit() Fit the cause-specific Cox model.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the cause-specific Cox model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_competing.py#L1724-L1880){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit( surv, covariates=None, *, data=None, strata=None, robust=False, cluster=None, frailty=None, frailty_cluster=None, frailty_theta=0.5, frailty_max_iter=30, max_iter=30, tol=1e-09, weights=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Re-codes the multi-state response so that the target cause is treated as the event and all competing causes are treated as censored, then fits a standard `CoxPH` model on the re-coded data. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A multi-state response: a `Surv` with a categorical event, an `Outcome` (such as `gw.Outcome.first_event(...)`), or a formula string such as `"Surv(etime, factor(cause, c(0, 1, 2), c('censor', 'pcm', 'death'))) ~ age + sex"`. An `Outcome` or formula reads its columns from `data`. The formula's right-hand side sets `covariates`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe or 2-D array of covariates. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response, `strata`, `cluster`, `frailty_cluster`, and `covariates`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. [strata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [robust]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [cluster]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [frailty]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [frailty_cluster]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [frailty_theta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [frailty_max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Newton-Raphson iteration control passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Newton-Raphson iteration control passed through to `CoxPH.fit()`. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Case weights, one per row (a column name in `data`, or an array). Must be finite and strictly positive. Default is `None` (all weights `1`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [CauseSpecificCox]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a cause-specific Cox model for plasma-cell malignancy (pcm) in the `mgus2` dataset. Competing events (death) are treated as censored: ::: {#3309d6fc .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw mg = gw.load_dataset("mgus2", backend="pandas") cr = gw.Outcome.first_event( endpoints={"pcm": ("ptime", "pstat"), "death": ("futime", "death")} ) csc = gw.CauseSpecificCox(cause="pcm").fit( cr, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=mg ) csc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` CauseSpecificCox (cause-specific Cox model, cause='pcm', ties='efron') coef exp(coef) se(coef) z p age 0.01304 1.013 0.008259 1.579 0.1144 sexM -0.02514 0.9752 0.1885 -0.133 0.8939 n = 1384, events = 115 Likelihood ratio test = 2.682 on 2 df, p = 0.2616 ``` ::: ::: Exponentiated coefficients give cause-specific hazard ratios: ::: {#5d9f4d45 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.tidy(csc, exponentiate=True, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
